source.title: Causal dictionary learning reveals and validates transcription-factor binding features in genomic language models

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse dictionary learning and feature validation to genomic language models, a new setting, and reports results on recovered and causally tested features.
record.gate_note: Layer selection and training settings are reported but are not treated as findings about the claim. Results cited from other studies are not included. The paper's own results on sparse feature recovery, motif validation, and causal ablation are recorded.
record.test_reason: Trains top-k SAEs on two genomic masked language models, a new setting. It reports that sparse dictionaries reconstruct activations and recover motif- and binding-related features, some causally used. This bears on V4. It does not test completeness, stability or canonicality of the dictionary (V5), toy-model geometry (V1), capacity mechanisms (V2/V3) or feature dimensionality (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that top-k SAEs on two genomic LMs recover monosemantic, motif-aligned features, and that naive PWM validation is dominated by GC/repeat confounds. They find that composition-matched testing plus forward-pass ablation shows selected features are causally used for TF binding (7–14 of 15 per condition), with null results under scrambled-label and random-feature controls. They add that GATA1 binding is encoded through context beyond the canonical motif, which only the causal test reveals.
record.recipe_differences: Uses top-k sparse autoencoders on pretrained genomic language-model activations and validates feature directions through ChIP-seq comparisons and forward-pass ablation; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports layer dependence: intermediate layers gave the best reconstruction/live-feature balance, and subsequent analyses used NT layer 14 and DNABERT-2 layer 6. Motif-selectivity varied by transcription factor, and binding-feature counts differed across models and factors.

fits_no_version.finding: Naive PWM enrichment flagged 440 of 6,576 features as CTCF-enriched. The top features tracked Alu repeats, GC-rich or CpG-island sequence, and their enrichment collapsed under GC matching.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature interpretations obtained by correlational motif enrichment are largely confounded by sequence composition in genomic LMs.

fits_no_version.finding: A motif-selective, non-binding feature had an ablation effect about 10× larger than a binding feature but chance binding specificity (AUC 0.51 vs 0.63).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A feature's causal importance and its specificity to a concept dissociate under SAE-direction ablation.

record.problems: Only two masked-language-model encoders and three transcription factors were examined. The study tests selected features rather than completeness or stability of the dictionaries; model-specific values are not given for the aggregate reconstruction range. Some reported figure results lack numerical values.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, overlap geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
All: polysemanticity is only cited, not measured.
Whether features are spread across many neurons: no neuron-level polysemanticity measurement. Only two genomic masked-LM encoders, one layer each, for the downstream analyses.
Completeness, stability across seeds/sizes, and canonicality of SAE features. The 74–76% variance explained is reported but not analysed as a completeness test.
All: no comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Layer dependence of SAE reconstruction and live-feature fraction across four sampled layers per model, peaking at intermediate depth (no numbers given).
Initializing dictionaries from data raised the live-feature fraction from 45% to 93% at fixed reconstruction error. This is a training-choice sensitivity of dictionary recovery.
NT layer 14: 'only a small number' of the 265 CTCF motif-selective features stayed binding-sensitive after GC control; no count given.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is mainly a validation-method paper that uses SAEs as a tool. It bears on V4 only because it reports that sparse dictionaries recover interpretable, causally used features in a new domain. The cited Toy Models paper appears only as background for polysemanticity. The causal counts are for pre-selected top-15 candidates, not population rates. The reader's V5 links and labels were removed because nothing tests completeness, stability or canonicality. The reader's V4 limits_scope label based on negative controls was dropped: the controls validate the method rather than limit the claim. Single-author preprint with no code release stated.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric structure.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by competition for limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
The study examines two genomic masked-language-model encoders, not other LLM families or modalities; it does not measure feature distribution across neurons.

The study validates selected feature interpretations, but does not test whether the dictionary is complete, whether features are stable across runs or settings, or whether SAE features are canonical units.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional feature representations or superposition geometry.

relationships.condition: NT v2 layer 14 and DNABERT-2 layer 6; CTCF and REST, plus GATA1 causal tests
relationships.reason: k=32 SAEs explain 74–76% of variance (r1). Hundreds of CTCF/REST motif-selective features (r2, r4, r5, r7). 7–14/15 selected features are causally binding-specific vs 0/15 random (r8–r14). Exemplar features show graded activation (r24, r25).
relationships.display_finding: k=32 SAEs explained 74–76% of variance and yielded hundreds of CTCF- and REST-selective features. Between 7 and 14 of 15 selected features were causally binding-specific against 0 of 15 random ones, and exemplar features showed graded activation.
